newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Chretien sees definite health spending.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Chretien sees definite health spending.

text.p: Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien pledged on Wednesday that the new health spending that he announced on Monday would proceed regardless of the state of the country's finances.

He and Industry Minister John Manley pointed to the fact that the Liberal government had consistently done better than its deficit targets. But pressed by a reporter on whether the new health spending would proceed no matter what, he said: Yes, it's a commitment of the government that we do, like all the other programs of the government."
On Monday, Chretien announced that the government would reverse C$4.8 billion in planned cuts in transfers to the provinces for health and social spending over the next five years.

Asked if the same commitment would apply to the new electoral platform's commitment to double, "as resources become available," the C$850 million increase that has been made to the new Canada Child Tax Benefit, he said no.
"It's of a different nature," he said, referring to the conditional clause in the platform, dubbed Red Book Two.
"If we were to go into a deep recession next two years, we will not be proceeding with that."
He made his remarks at a news conference in Saskatoon as he released his new Red Book. On Sunday Chretien called a June 2 election after 3-1/2 years in office.
